summary:
Rather than relying on dry technical specifications, this concept treats retired space artifacts as off-world archaeological sites and characters with emotional legacies, bridging historic missions with future ones like Artemis.
The deck highlights key hardware "characters" and structures their stories into three first-person acts:
• The Cast: Lunar artifacts include Apollo descent stages, ALSEP science stations, and personal human keepsakes like Alan Shepard’s golf balls. Martian hardware includes the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, entry and descent debris, and the Ingenuity helicopter.
• Narrative Blueprint: Stories follow Act I: The Awakening (arrival and purpose), Act II: The Discovery (overcoming hazards to make breakthroughs), and Act III: The Long Watch (fading batteries and waiting for future astronauts).
• Engagement Formats: Recended deliverables include an interactive 3D "Ghost Map" with audio postcards, illustrated comic field guides, and hands-on STEM classroom challenges
details: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is an interactive storytelling and STEM education concept designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. By giving a first-person voice to NASA’s dormant lunar and Martian hardware—from Apollo landers to Mars rovers—the project transforms over 50 years of off-world engineering into relatable adventures. Through clickable 3D globes, audio postcards, illustrated field guides, and classroom activities, it connects the legacy of past space exploration with the next generation of explorers.
